Perfect substitutes (linear) functions

Source: R/utilities.R
perfect_substitutes.Rd

Builds \(f(x, y) = A (a x + b y)\): straight-line contours with constant MRS \(a / b\). The consumer spends everything on whichever good gives more utility per unit of money, so the optimum is a corner unless \(a / p_x = b / p_y\) exactly, when every point on the budget line is equally good. In that knife-edge case optimal_bundle() returns the midpoint of the budget line and flags the result with an indeterminate attribute set to TRUE. "Exactly" means within all.equal()'s default tolerance, about 1.5e-8 relative: two utilities-per-dollar that differ only in the ninth significant figure count as a tie.

Usage

perfect_substitutes(a = 1, b = 1, A = 1, kind = c("utility", "production"))

Arguments

a, b

Marginal utility of x and y. Positive. (b here is the textbook coefficient, not a budget() – the letter is kept because that is how the formula is written.)

A

Scale factor. Positive.

kind

"utility" or "production".

Value

A function of x and y of class perfect_substitutes, with a, b, A and kind as attributes.

Examples

u <- perfect_substitutes(a = 1, b = 2)   # y is worth twice x
optimal_bundle(u, budget(100, 1, 1))     # all y
#>   x   y utility
#> 1 0 100     200
optimal_bundle(u, budget(100, 1, 3))     # all x
#>     x y utility
#> 1 100 0     100
attr(optimal_bundle(u, budget(100, 1, 2)), "indeterminate")
#> [1] TRUE
